limitations: The Texas boundary is a geographic constraint, not an official ERCOT footprint.
The boundary asset's small disconnected coastal/island ring is excluded from the contiguous mainland planning footprint.
The 0.1-degree raster is a reproducibility device; boundaries are not official zones.
Public crossing evidence is not electrical connectivity or thermal capacity.
Load allocation remains a future teaching-scenario assumption.

method.contiguity_repair: disconnected non-primary raster components are reassigned to the adjacent region with the strongest shared edge, then nearest-seed tie break
method.feature_normalization: geography is the hard assignment constraint; public evidence is summarized after assignment and does not override spatial coherence
method.topology_policy: No endpoint merging, line-crossing connectivity, electrical bus identity, impedance, ratings, or MW limits are inferred.

metrics.footprint: largest mainland ring from Texas boundary asset; not an ERCOT boundary
